summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,677.28, up 0.32%, with the Nasdaq 100 leading at +0.62% as technology reclaimed the wheel ahead of NVIDIA's earnings report after the close on Wednesday. The 10 year yield fell to 4.64%, down 1.38%, pulling TLT up 1.10% to 83.47 as oil dropped another 4.72% to 81.00 on Iran diplomacy progress around the Strait of Hormuz, keeping the bond friendly picture intact for a second straight session. Gold extended its rally to 4,716.10, up 1.62%, copper added 1.75%, while Bitcoin slipped to 78,219.04, down 0.94%, and Ethereum fell 1.79%. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on 27.6 billion dollars of US goods, MRNA surged 14.4% on cancer vaccine news, and INTU sank roughly 3.4% after a weak outlook. The fear and greed index sits at 59, greed, up from 55 a week ago and 41 a month ago. Wednesday brings Core PCE, preliminary GDP, and NVIDIA earnings, all of which could define the week's direction.
